name: Platform Login / MFA

transitions.trigger: A partner user signs in through the same door

notes: **Rebuilt as a sign-in form on 2 October 2026 (CHG-DOOR-002/003; Chinmay, 2 October 2026: fix the Block A blockers now).** It was generated as a list over active sessions, MFA methods and SSO providers with Force logout and Revoke all sessions on the door, which a person who is not yet signed in can never use (platform-foundation process notes). The sequence is the same on every staff and partner door: credentials (or the organisation's SSO) -> the authentication code only when a permission demands it (R135) -> the role prompt when several roles are held (ADR-0003) -> the landing. Managing sessions moved to the staff directory (BO-053); managing MFA methods stays on each app's own security or profile screen. **Every platform operator holds a PLATFORM_* permission, so the code is always asked** and the first sign-in always enrols (F104). Platform operators' sessions are not listed here: a session list on the Console would call tenant-permission operations with no platform-staff grant (R098).
patternReason: A sign-in: two fields, the organisation's SSO where configured, and the second-factor and role steps in place - a form, not a list to browse.
purpose: Get a TICVAI platform operator into the TICVAI Console: username and password (or TICVAI's own SSO), then always the authentication code, then the Platform Dashboard.

components.label: Username
components.notes: Goes into `LoginRequest.username`.

components.label: Password
components.notes: Goes into `LoginRequest.credential` with `method: password`. Minimum 8, show/hide. **No workstation is sent: a browser is not a registered device** (CHG-DOOR-001), and no PIN is offered, because a PIN is bounded by a device this door does not have.

components.label: Sign in
components.notes: Sends `LoginRequest`. 409 means this person already holds a session elsewhere (audit R184): the screen says where and since when, and that only a holder of SESSION_FORCE_LOGOUT can end it; signing in never ends the other session.

components.label: Sign in with your organisation
components.notes: One button per identity provider TICVAI uses for its own staff; **absent, not disabled, when there is none.** Read before sign-in, unauthenticated. When a provider `isEnforced` for this person, the password field is hidden and only this remains.

components.label: Continue with your organisation
components.notes: Hands off to the identity provider with this door's `redirectUri`; nothing is typed here. Staff and partner doors only, never a guest door (audit R167).

components.label: Finishing sign-in with your organisation
components.notes: On the provider's redirect back (`code` and `state` from the redirect, never typed). Returns the same `LoginResponse` as `login`, so the second factor and the role prompt follow exactly as below. 403: the provider proved who this is and no group maps to a role in this tenant, which grants nothing.

components.label: Authentication code
components.notes: Shown only when the sign-in comes back `requiresMfa`: the person holds a permission in `PasswordPolicy.mfaRequiredForPermissions` (ROLE_MANAGE, LEDGER_APPROVE, every PLATFORM_* permission, or one the tenant added; audit R135). Six digits from the authenticator app.

components.label: Verify
components.notes: Completes the sign-in; the session is usable only after it. Five wrong codes lock step-up for the policy's lockout minutes, never permanently (audit R126 (6)), and the screen says until when.

components.label: Email me a code instead
components.notes: `action: signIn`. The authenticator app is the primary method and an emailed code the fallback (audit R126 (5)).

components.label: Set up the authenticator app
components.notes: Only when the sign-in comes back `requiresMfa` with `hasMfaMethod: false`: the first method is enrolled here before anything else (audit R135). Authenticator app (`totp`) or email (`emailOtp`) only; the secret as QR and text.

components.label: Recovery codes
components.notes: The method is active once its first code is verified. Recovery codes are shown once, with copy and download, and never again.

components.label: Signed in as
components.notes: Read once the sign-in is complete (after the code and the role, where asked): the person's name and role, then straight on. A platform operator lands on the Platform Dashboard (ADM-002).

components.label: Choose role
components.notes: Only when `LoginResponse.requiresRoleSelection` is true: large role buttons, one per role the person holds (ADR-0003). One role goes straight in. A platform operator lands on the Platform Dashboard (ADM-002).

components.label: New password
components.notes: Only when the credential was reset and is temporary: a new one is set before anything else, twice, and the last five cannot be reused (audit R132).

states.loading: Checking the credential. The form stays visible and disabled.
states.emptyFirstRun: **Nobody signed in** - the normal state of a door. The form offers username and password and, where TICVAI uses one, its SSO.
states.error: Identity could not be reached. **Says so rather than saying the password is wrong**, and keeps what was typed.
states.denied: The credential does not match, or the account is locked. One message for both, with the attempts left before the lock; a locked account says when to try again.
states.emptyNoAccess: Signed in, and the person holds no role in this app. Says who at the tenant grants access; distinct from a wrong password. A door has no permission of its own to name, because the person is not signed in until it succeeds.
states.emptyNoResults: Never shown: `listSsoProviders` takes no filter; a tenant with no identity provider shows no SSO buttons at all, and the form is the whole door.
states.sessionHeld: `login` answered 409: this person already holds a session elsewhere (audit R184, ADR-0004). Says where and since when; only a holder of SESSION_FORCE_LOGOUT ends it, on the staff directory (BO-053), and signing in never ends it by itself.
states.mfaRequired: **Signed in, not yet through.** The principal holds a permission that requires MFA (ROLE_MANAGE, LEDGER_APPROVE, any PLATFORM_* permission, or one the tenant added), so the screen calls `createMfaChallenge` (`action: signIn`) and asks for the authentication code; `verifyMfaChallenge` completes the sign-in. **Email me a code instead** is the fallback. Five wrong codes lock step-up for the policy's lockout minutes and the screen says until when (audit R135, R126). A person without such a permission never reaches this state.
states.mfaEnrolmentRequired: **First sign-in, no method yet.** A person who requires MFA and has no active method enrols the authenticator app (email as the fallback) with `enrolMfaMethod`, confirms it with the first code (`verifyMfaEnrolment`), sees the recovery codes once, then continues to the code step (audit R135, R126 (5)).
states.offline: Not available, and the offline banner says why: signing in needs a connection.

Hand off to the identity provider where the tenant has SSO

Second factor after sign-in when the principal holds a permission in mfaRequiredForPermissions; action `signIn`, the authenticator app, or the email method as the fallback (audit R135, R126 (5))
Completes sign-in with the code; the session is usable only after it. Five wrong codes lock step-up (audit R126 (6))
The first method, at a first sign-in that requires one: authenticator app, or email as the fallback (audit R135, R126 (5))
Activates the enrolled method with its first code; recovery codes shown once
Choose which role to work as when sign-in returns more than one (ADR-0003)
Replace a temporary password or PIN at the first sign-in after a reset (audit R132)
Read the session the sign-in just opened, for the landing

entryState.coldEntry: **Needs nothing; that is what makes it the door.** No workstation travels with a browser sign-in (CHG-DOOR-001). `providerId` arrives only on the identity provider's redirect back, with the `code` and `state` that `completeSsoAuthorization` exchanges; an expired or replayed redirect lands on the form with "That sign-in link has expired; sign in again".

apisNote: Declared by hand on 2 October 2026 (CHG-DOOR-002/003): sign-in, SSO, the second factor and its first enrolment, the role prompt, a temporary credential's replacement and the session read for the landing. Nothing that needs a signed-in session to list or end sessions is here.

**Tenant picker and platform-staff grant added 2 October 2026** (CHG-SBO-001; Chinmay, pre-apply round: console screens get the R098 tenant picker and grant, the ADM-412 pattern). The Console runs outside every cell; `listPrincipals` (USER_MANAGE), `createPrincipal` (USER_MANAGE), `getPrincipal` (USER_MANAGE), `updatePrincipal` (USER_MANAGE) are tenant operations, refused 403 to a platform token until a time-boxed, audited grant into the picked tenant is open. components.label: Tenant
components.notes: **Pick a tenant first** (audit R098; decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay: console screens get the tenant picker and grant, CHG-SBO-001). This screen's operations run in that tenant's cell, and a platform token carries no tenant permission there until a platform-staff grant into it is open.

components.label: Open grant into this tenant
components.notes: **Always visible while the screen acts on a tenant** (audit R098, the ADM-412 pattern): which tenant, which permissions, why, and the time left to `expiresAt`. At expiry every tenant action is disabled and the screen returns to its grantRequired state; a new need is a new grant. The tenant sees the grant in its own audit log. Found again after a reload with `listOwnPlatformStaffGrants`.

components.label: Open access grant
components.notes: Shown until a grant into the picked tenant is open; asks for the second factor first (step-up, audit R135).

components.label: Scope path
components.notes: Sends `?scopePath=` to `listPrincipals`.

components.label: Is active
components.notes: Sends `?isActive=` to `listPrincipals`.

states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed and leaves the platform user untouched.
states.emptyFirstRun: No platform user yet. Offers Create principal (`createPrincipal`); distinct from a filter that matched nothing.
states.emptyNoResults: Nothing matches the filter on scopePath, isActive and the platform user are still there. Names the active filter and offers to clear it.
states.emptyNoAccess: Shown when the caller lacks `USER_MANAGE`, which `listPrincipals` requires to show this screen, and names that permission (the screen's other reads need `PLATFORM_TENANT_VIEW` and say so in their own panels). **Never an empty table** — that reads as *there is no data* and sends somebody to support with the wrong question. A caller who can see the screen but lacks what an action needs sees that action disabled, naming its permission: `PLATFORM_TENANT_ACCESS` for `listOwnPlatformStaffGrants`, `openPlatformStaffGrant`.
states.grantRequired: **No access into this tenant yet.** A tenant is picked and no platform-staff grant into it is open, so every tenant action is disabled and the screen offers **Open access grant** (`openPlatformStaffGrant`: reason, permissions `USER_MANAGE`, expiry). The same state returns when the grant reaches `expiresAt` (audit R098; CHG-SBO-001).

overlays.body: **Collects what `createPrincipal` sends before it is called.** Required: `username`, `displayName`. Optional: `initialCredential`, `mustChangeCredential`, `validTo`, `roleIds`. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

**Collects what `updatePrincipal` sends before it is called.** Nothing in the body is required. Optional: `displayName`, `isActive`, `validTo`, `primaryRoleId`. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

**Collects what `openPlatformStaffGrant` sends before it is called** (audit R098). Required: `id` (a client UUIDv7, generated silently), `permissions` (tenant permissions only; `USER_MANAGE` preselected for this screen), `reason`, `expiresAt` (at most 8 hours ahead, proposed). Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

name: My Account & Security

transitions.trigger: Signing this session out returns to the door

notes: **Added 2 October 2026** (Chinmay, door follow-ups: "Add 'My account & security'"; CHG-SBO-022, CHG-CSP-052). A platform operator's own second-factor methods and own sessions. The doors no longer manage them (CHG-DOOR-002, CHG-DOOR-003), and the staff session list (`listActiveSessions`) needs `SESSION_FORCE_LOGOUT`, which an operator should not need to see their own sessions. **Nothing here needs a permission**: every signed-in operator sees only their own account, and ending a session or removing a method asks for the authentication code first. **No tenant picker**: the operator's account is the Control Plane's, not a tenant's (R098 does not apply).
patternReason: Two short lists the operator acts on, their own methods and their own sessions, with the account they are signed in as above them.
purpose: Let a platform operator manage their own sign-in: the authentication methods, the password and the sessions they hold, and sign any of those sessions out.

components.label: This session
components.notes: The operator's own account and the session in use (marked in the list below); never another operator's.

components.label: Authentication methods
components.notes: The authenticator app is the method; the emailed code is the fallback. Every platform operator holds a PLATFORM_* permission, so at least one method always stays: removing the last one is refused and the button is disabled with that reason.

components.label: My sessions
components.notes: Every session this operator holds, this one marked "This session". Paged (`listOwnSessions`).

components.label: Add a method
components.notes: Starts enrolling an authenticator app or an email fallback; the code is confirmed next.

components.label: Confirm the code
components.notes: Finishes enrolment with the six-digit code.

components.label: Remove method
components.notes: Asks for the authentication code first; never the last method.

components.label: Sign this session out
components.notes: Ends one of the operator's own sessions after a fresh second factor (`endOwnSession` is step-up mfa); ending the current one returns to the door.

overlays.body: **Collects what `enrolMfaMethod` sends before it is called.** Required: `kind`. Optional: `target`. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.
**Collects what `verifyMfaEnrolment` sends before it is called.** Required: `code`. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

**Collects what `changeOwnCredential` sends before it is called.** Required: `method`, `currentCredential`, `newCredential`. The current password is asked; the new one meets the password policy (minimum 8). Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.
Names the device and when the session started, then asks for the authentication code (`createMfaChallenge`, `verifyMfaChallenge`) before `endOwnSession` is sent. Dismissing sends nothing.
Names the method, asks for the authentication code first (`createMfaChallenge`), and is refused for the last method.

states.loading: The account, its methods and its sessions.
states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed (methods or sessions) and leaves the other in place.
states.emptyFirstRun: **Never empty for methods**: the first sign-in enrols one (F104). With one session, the list shows only "This session" and says no other session is open.
states.emptyNoResults: Never shown: nothing on this screen filters.
states.emptyNoAccess: Never shown: every signed-in operator sees their own account; nothing here needs a permission.
states.stepUp: Ending a session and removing a method ask for the authentication code in the confirmation (`createMfaChallenge`, `verifyMfaChallenge`); five wrong codes lock step-up for the lockout minutes, never permanently.
